testName: ICT2613 · May/June 2018 exam · source-linked practice (not verbatim)
sourceType: Source-verified topics, original practice questions (not the original exam text)
sourceLimitations: Verified 2018 examination source is publicly listed. These are rewritten practice questions following the paper's topic order, not a verbatim copy of copyrighted questions. Open the linked original to see exact wording.

questions.text: Which answer best distinguishes a web server from a web browser?
options: The server sends web resources; the browser requests and shows them
The browser stores MySQL tables; the server creates charts
Both always perform the exact same role
The server is another name for a search engine
questions.correctAnswer: The server sends web resources; the browser requests and shows them
questions.explanation:
Browsers request pages using HTTP or HTTPS; servers respond with content.

Student note: Apache is a web server and Chrome is a web browser.

questions.text: Which option gives a web server followed by a browser?
questions.explanation:
Apache handles web requests, and Firefox displays webpages.

Student note: Software roles matter more than brand names: browser, server, scripting engine, database.

questions.text: Which description fits a dynamic webpage?
options: Its response may change based on code, stored data or user input
Its content must always be exactly the same HTML
It does not use any server
questions.correctAnswer: Its response may change based on code, stored data or user input
questions.explanation:
A dynamic page can generate different responses at request time.

Student note: Dynamic PHP pages can show database records; static pages usually serve stored content as-is.

questions.text: Which group of tools could be used to build and test a PHP site on a local computer?
options: Code editor, Apache/PHP, MySQL and a browser
Calculator, Paint, PowerPoint and a scanner
Browser alone without a PHP runtime
questions.correctAnswer: Code editor, Apache/PHP, MySQL and a browser
questions.explanation:
The editor writes code; web/PHP server runs it; MySQL stores data; browser displays results.

Student note: XAMPP bundles several development services, but it is not itself a browser.

questions.text: Create PHP values for a student name, number of modules, registration price per module (constant) and a final-year yes/no flag. Use camelCase for variable names.
questions.explanation:
String, integer, numeric constant and boolean values serve different purposes.

Student note: Use true/false for boolean values; constants should not change while the program runs.

questions.text: Using $moduleCount and REGISTRATION_PRICE, store the total registration cost in $totalFees.
questions.explanation:
Total cost is the quantity multiplied by the price per module.

Student note: Do not add the same price just once; multiply by the number of modules.

questions.text: Use the ternary operator to set $yearLabel to 'FY student' if $isFinalYear is true, otherwise to 'Not FY student'.
questions.explanation:
A ternary expression chooses between two values depending on a condition.

Student note: Syntax: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse.

questions.text: Display the student's name, total fees and final-year label together as an HTML paragraph using PHP echo.
questions.explanation:
Concatenation joins strings and variables into one output.

Student note: The dot (.) concatenates PHP strings; escape user-provided text before displaying in HTML.

questions.text: Build three radio buttons sharing one field name called preference, with values email, cellphone and post. Put them inside a GET form that goes to preference.php.
questions.correctAnswer:
<form action="preference.php" method="get">
  <label><input type="radio" name="preference" value="email">Email</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="preference" value="cellphone">Cellphone</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="preference" value="post">Post</label>
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
questions.explanation:
A shared name groups radio options into one choice.

Student note: Radio group values are what PHP receives, not necessarily the visible labels.

questions.text: A form uses action='preference.php'. Which script will receive the submitted data?
questions.explanation:
The action attribute names the form handler.

Student note: The method attribute separately decides whether GET or POST carries the values.

questions.text: Write a PHP function mailDescription() that echoes Fast mail for email, Expensive for cellphone and Slow mail for post, using if/else logic.
questions.explanation:
An if/else chain tests alternatives in order and runs the matching branch.

Student note: Use === when you want exact equality, including the same type.

questions.text: Read the preference value from a GET request and call mailDescription() if the value is present.
questions.explanation:
GET form fields are available from $_GET or filter_input(INPUT_GET, ...).

Student note: Match the form's method: $_POST is not interchangeable with $_GET.

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes PHP '=' compared with '=='?
options: == creates a constant and = checks identity
questions.explanation:
Assignment changes a variable, while equality checks whether values compare equal.

Student note: === checks both value and type; it differs from ==.

questions.text: When combining two boolean conditions in PHP, what does && mean?
options: At least one must be true
questions.explanation:
Logical AND requires true on both sides, whereas logical OR (||) needs at least one.

Student note: Make a truth table to learn AND, OR and NOT.

questions.text: A PHP switch marks days 1 and 7 as Rest day, days 2 through 6 as Work day and all other values as Invalid day. What is shown for 1, 100, 5 and 7?
options: Rest day, Invalid day, Work day, Rest day
Rest day, Work day, Invalid day, Rest day
Work day, Invalid day, Work day, Rest day
Invalid day, Invalid day, Rest day, Work day
questions.correctAnswer: Rest day, Invalid day, Work day, Rest day
questions.explanation:
The matching case sets the label; unmatched 100 uses default.

Student note: Remember break statements to avoid unintended fall-through.

questions.text: Write a for loop that counts how many strings in $list have more than 10 characters. Store the result in $longCount.
aiRubric: Counts strings longer than ten only
questions.explanation:
strlen() returns a length that you can compare with 10.

Student note: More than 10 means > 10, not >= 10.

questions.text: Given a connected PDO object $db and a modules table, write PHP that selects code and name columns and displays each result on its own line.
questions.explanation:
SELECT retrieves columns; fetchAll or repeated fetch retrieves matching records.

Student note: Escape database content when printing it as HTML.

questions.text: A module code is stored in $moduleCode. Write a PDO prepared statement to delete only that code's record from modules.
questions.explanation:
DELETE with WHERE targets rows meeting its condition.

Student note: Never omit WHERE from a targeted delete; a prepared statement helps protect SQL input.

questions.text: Which PHP expression can produce today's date on the server?
questions.explanation:
date() formats the current date and time using a pattern.

Student note: Y means four-digit year, m is month and d is day. Server timezone affects the date.

questions.text: What are cookies normally used for?
options: Keeping small browser-side values across requests
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping small browser-side values across requests
questions.explanation:
Cookies can remember non-sensitive preferences or a session identifier.

Student note: Do not store passwords or sensitive secrets in ordinary cookies.

questions.text: How do PHP sessions usually remember a visitor between separate HTTP requests?
options: A session identifier links requests to stored session data
Each browser request automatically contains all server variables
HTTP permanently remembers every page visit without help
Sessions exist only inside CSS styles
questions.correctAnswer: A session identifier links requests to stored session data
questions.explanation:
HTTP is stateless; session IDs let the server associate later requests with one visitor.

Student note: session_start() begins or resumes a session; $_SESSION contains session values.
